Reduce the motivating factors for crime and you will reduce crime. Most of the motivating factors are socio-economic factors, but some are lifestyle choices and a few are mental-health oriented (which may never be eliminated but might be reduced).

A simple fact is that the richer someone is, the less reason they have to steal, while the poorer someone is, the more reason they have to steal. Same goes for criminal activity. Here I think the simplest solution is the best: eliminate poverty. How do you do that? Again, I think the simplest solution is best: give people enough money to meet their basic needs (a basic income), regardless of how much they need it. If they don't need the money because they have a job that pays well, either tax it back out of them or give them an incentive to spend or donate it so that it gets back into the economy. This concept also has the added benefit of solving the automation problem whereby jobs are increasingly eliminated. It also allows people to do whatever it is they really want to do, which can lead to all kinds of societal enhancements.

Another simple fact is that people are always going to try to do things they like doing, so there's little point in trying to stop them as long as what they like to do does not harm anyone else. Decriminalizing things like drugs is a great first step. Most people don't want to do drugs and never will even if it's made legal. Some people will continue to do drugs regardless of whether or not it's legal.

So free money and legal drugs is the answer. The question then is how to make that free money part work. While it's sure to be complicated in terms of getting the funding, the distribution is as simple as can be: anyone 18 and up gets the money. If you have dependents under the age of 18, you get an additional smaller amount of money for the first 2 dependents and nothing after that (gotta incentivize population stability after all).

And of course, the criminal "justice" system should be totally overhauled and geared towards rehabilitation and reintegration (if possible), rather than punishment. It's usually only the criminally insane who want to commit crimes. Those that don't need to be shown how to live without committing crimes, or how to manage their problems in a positive way.

This will all naturally take some massive cultural changes that I am afraid will never happen, of course. But it's a nice idea.
